name: Are You Quite Sure?
tagline: You got there first. You're still glad you did.
epigraph: A Sidecar without its lemon. The sour comes from the grape itself.
language_row: Wren's checks on v3: title block, whoYouAre and yours swap-tested against the family (in her turns); history share in yours 250 of 503 words (49.7%); lint 0 errors, 5 warnings (gendered pronouns in yours 1–5, Louis Pasteur, a historical person, accepted by Wren in r4). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/pasteur-biot-racemic-acid-1848.md`. René Vallery-Radot, *The Life of Pasteur*, tr. Mrs R. L. Devonshire (Doubleday, Page, 1920 printing; Project Gutenberg #60956), ch. II–III: secondary, period, by Pasteur's son-in-law; the Biot scene rests on Pasteur's own memory ("as Pasteur told it"). *The Cocktail Codex* p. 187 (verjus) and p. 195 (tartaric acid); *Liquid Intelligence* sour ranges. Web: Hester's library-first visits for the Gutenberg text.
names_note: Split 1–1–1 in round 4: *Are You Quite Sure?* (Wren), *Nothing Escaped You* (Tomás), *Before Your Eyes* (Hester). Wren and Tomás each wrote "I could take *Before Your Eyes*" (Hester wrote she could take *Are You Quite Sure?* in r3). Also considered: *Both Hands*, *Let Them Check*. The pour carries Wren's title-block name until Robin picks. Picks were held until the vote.
open_items: Name split 1–1–1, for Robin's pick (see Names considered).

Balance: balance.py reads the drink OUT on every stirred range (finished 15.9% / 6.26 g / 0.757%, dilution 35.8%). Tomás moved the spec to freeform with the stirring melt declared as a water line and judges it by hand against Arnold's shaken-sour ranges: strength and sugar in, acid an edge on the floor (0.757 vs 0.76). Kept by choice (r4 step 1).

Verjus acid (2.5%) and sugar (6 g) are unsourced standard values; the drink is proven only for a verjus of about 2.5–3.1% acid, and a softer bottle lands under the sour floor (fallback in Sweeps, out of guest text).
The colour ("almost colourless, faint pale-straw") is Tomás's estimate, unsourced.
